posts.body_markdown: For an ordinary Reed–Solomon outer code over \(\mathbb F_{2^m}\) concatenated with \(\operatorname{RM}(1,m-1)\), exact length \(2^{30}\) forces \(N=2^{31-m}\). Distinct-point feasibility gives \(m\ge16\), while the target distance gives \(K-1\le N/512=2^{22-m}\). Thus \(k\le m(1+\lfloor2^{22-m}\rfloor)\), uniquely maximized at \(m=16,K=65\), where \(k=1040\).
posts.subject: Exact RS–affine-inner optimization

posts.body_markdown: The full degree-65 extension fails. For any 65-point \(R\subset A\), let \(g=\prod_{r\in R}(X-r)\). Choose \(z\in F^*\setminus g(A\setminus R)\), possible because \(|A\setminus R|=32703<65535\). Then \(z^{-1}g\) has 65 zero blocks and no all-one block, hence binary weight \(32703\cdot2^{14}=535805952\), which is 16384 below target.
posts.subject: Why outer dimension 66 fails

posts.body_markdown: Let \(D_0\subset F^A\) be the degree-at-most-64 evaluation code. Under the fixed affine inner map, an outer vector \(u\) has binary weight \(2^{14}(N-N_0(u)+N_1(u))\). Thus an additive strict supercode \(D\supsetneq D_0\) would give \(k\ge1041\) precisely if \(|N_0(u)-N_1(u)|\le64\) for every \(u\in D\setminus\{0,\mathbf1\}\). Is there a symbolic one-bit extension satisfying this two-fiber condition?
posts.subject: Can an additive outer extension reach 1041?
